messages.subject: Doubt about partial invariance
parts:
Hello everyone
I am new to this topic, and a doubt arose when I was analyzing the results of a job I am doing. I have searched in different sources and clear examples and well, in them they take from lavTestScore() the values that can make a change in the invariance results and most of them put the following group.partial=c("itemX~1") in the code . However, in my case the values that I get in lavTestScore() and parTable() are with the following F1 =~ am15. And my question was if I put this in my code group.partial=c("F1=~am15"), would it be in the same way as group.partial=c("itemX~1") working as a partial invariance?
Other examples I saw were that their results with "~~" instead of "=~"

messages.subject: AW: Doubt about partial invariance
parts:
I am not sure if I understand your question correctly. On prueba2.png I can't find F1 =~ am15.
group.partial=c("F1=~am15") frees the factor loading. There is an example in the lavaan tutorial:

fit <- cfa(HS.model, 
           data = HolzingerSwineford1939, 
           group = "school",
           group.equal = c("loadings", "intercepts"),
           group.partial = c("visual=~x2", "x7~1"))
https://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/groups.html

HTH

Christian

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: Doubt about partial invariance
parts: The code  group.partial=c("itemX~1")  would relax an equality constraint on an intercept. So this might be someone who established metric or weak invariance, failed to get strong or metric invariance, and now is looking to settle for partial strong invariance. Your code  ("F1 =~ am15")  would relax a constraint on a loading, so you would be giving up on full weak or metric invariance and trying to establish partial weak invariance. That would be the difference.
